title: fix(rest): the /meta state route tells a wired-and-failing engine apart from an absent one
body:
Fixes #15405

Clause-②: no

`objectQLProvider` has **two** consumers in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`. The engine-slot repair landed for one of them (#13476, the `computeExecCtx` authorization-input seam, reached through `wiredEngineOrLoud`). The other, `GET {basePath}/meta/object/:name/state/:field`, reached the same provider through `.catch(() => undefined)` and converted every rejection straight back into the `undefined` a never-registered engine produces, three lines before the answer is chosen. So an engine that was **wired and failed to build** and an engine that was **never registered** both answered `404 NOT_FOUND · "Object not found"` — a diagnostic route lying about the cause during exactly the incident it would be consulted in.

That line was **newly** load-bearing rather than long-broken. Before #13904 the shipped provider was `try { ... } catch { return undefined; }` and could not reject at all, so the `.catch` was dead code and the collapse happened one layer earlier. #13904 made the provider re-raise precisely so a consumer could see the outage. This consumer caught it back.

This is not rework on #13904 and touches nothing it pinned.

## The change — two call sites in one file

| site | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET {basePath}/meta/object/:name/state/:field` | `this.objectQLProvider(environmentId).catch(() => undefined)` | `wiredEngineOrLoud(Boolean(this.objectQLProvider), () => this.objectQLProvider!(environmentId))` |
| `POST {basePath}/email/send` | `this.emailServiceProvider(environmentId).catch(() => undefined)` | `seamOrUndefined(() => this.emailServiceProvider!(environmentId))` |

⭐ **`wiredEngineOrLoud`, not `seamOrUndefined`, at the engine seam** — deliberately, and against the dispatch's own generic wording. `seamOrUndefined`'s docblock forbids it in as many words: *"⛔ Do not route the data-engine seam back through this helper to 'make the seams uniform' — uniformity there IS the defect #13476 repaired."* `wiredEngineOrLoud` is what the sibling consumer already uses, so this route now gives the answer its sibling gives rather than a third one. Both helpers invoke the provider **synchronously**, which is the other half of the card: a `.catch` attaches to the promise the call *returns*, so a host wiring a non-`async` provider throws before any promise exists and the handler is never reached.

## ⚠️ Reachability — a correction to the card, measured rather than reasoned

The card does not say which wiring reaches this consumer, and the answer narrows its claim. Every `/meta` route is wrapped by `registerMetadataEndpoints`'s anonymous-deny gate, and **that gate resolves the same engine first**, through `computeExecCtx`. Its two branches do not agree:

| gate's engine branch | on a broken engine |
|:--|:--|
| PROVIDER branch (`wiredEngineOrLoud`, no `kernelManager` wired) | **raises** — this route's own engine line is never reached |
| KERNEL branch (`seamOrUndefined`, absorbing on purpose — `wiredEngineOrLoud`'s RESIDUE note) | **absorbs** — this route decides ⇐ the defect |

⇒ the collapse was reachable exactly where a resolvable kernel supplies auth and the separately-wired `objectQLProvider` is broken: the **multi-kernel** wiring (`rest-api-plugin.ts` wires a `kernelManager` when the host registers one). It was **not** reachable in a single-kernel boot such as `pnpm dev:crm`, where the gate raises first. Measured on a real `ObjectKernel`, not inferred; §0 of the new test file pins the property (not today's exact raise shape, which belongs to another door).

## What moves and what does not

Driven end to end on a real `RestServer` and a real `ObjectKernel` — nothing private is replaced, no fault is simulated by throwing a hand-made branded error into a stub:

| engine fact | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| no `objectQLProvider` wired at all | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | 404 `NOT_FOUND` — unchanged ⭐ PIN |
| provider RESOLVES `undefined` (the seam contract declaring absence) | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | 404 `NOT_FOUND` — unchanged ⭐ PIN |
| healthy engine, object that genuinely does not exist | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | 404 `NOT_FOUND` — unchanged ⭐ NEGATIVE CONTROL |
| healthy engine, object that exists | 200 | 200 — unchanged |
| provider REJECTS (wired, failed to build) | **404 `NOT_FOUND`** | **503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`** |
| provider THROWS SYNCHRONOUSLY (non-`async` host, #13280) | **500** | **503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`** |

⭐ **The pins assert the DISTINCTION, not a status code.** A build answering 503 for a broken engine *and* for a never-registered one would satisfy every bare `expect(status).toBe(503)` while telling a new lie, so the table above is asserted side by side with an explicit inequality (`[404, 404, 503]`, `new Set(...).size === 2`, and the codes differing). §4 goes further and derives the expected value **off the sibling seam's own error object** on the same fault, rather than writing a second literal beside it.

⚠️ **Envelope, so nobody reads it as a second defect.** The 503 arrives as the flat `{ error: 'Internal server error', code }` every withheld 5xx on this server wears (`handleRouteError`, #5437), while the sibling package door emits its own nested `{ error: { code } }`. The two doors agree on the pair that is the contract — status and machine code — and differ only in which emitter dresses it. That flat shape is pre-existing and pinned elsewhere (`rest-server-meta-read-org-scope.test.ts` names it verbatim); not this card's to move. `pnpm check:route-envelope` is green.

⚠️ **`POST /email/send` carries only the second observation.** No 404/503 question, and **not reachable from the shipped wiring** — both providers in `rest-api-plugin.ts` are declared `async`. Its answer is deliberately unchanged at `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; what changes is that the synchronous fault shape now reaches that same 501 instead of escaping past a `.catch` that did not exist yet and landing in the handler's own `500 EMAIL_SEND_FAILED`. Repaired because it is the same retired spelling at an embedder-reachable seam, not on a claim of live impact.

## Ablation — predicted in writing first, then run

Both legs mutate the committed tree, prove the mutation reached disk (marker counts **and** blob hash), run the pins, restore, and prove the restore by blob-hash equality **plus** an empty `git diff HEAD`. Restore is `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` under a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths. No `git stash`.

**Predicted, before running:** leg A red on the 3 cases in §2 plus the 1 in §4 (4 failed / 10 passed); leg B red on the §5 sync-throw case only (1 failed / 13 passed).

**Observed:**

| leg | mutation reached disk | result | the cases that went red |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A — restore `.catch(() => undefined)` at `objectQLProvider` | injected marker 0→1, deleted marker 1→0; blob `f384ecf5` → `c702672d` | **4 failed / 10 passed** | §2 rejecting (`expected 404 to be 503`), §2 sync-throw (`expected 500 to be 503`), §2 distinction (`[404,404,404]` vs `[404,404,503]`), §4 sibling agreement (`expected 404 to be 503`) |
| B — restore `.catch(() => undefined)` at `emailServiceProvider` | injected marker 0→1, deleted marker 1→0; blob `f384ecf5` → `df3a6ade` | **1 failed / 13 passed** | §5 sync-throw (`expected 500 to be 501`) |

Both legs restored to blob `f384ecf5d419b224d6b9932805a6df2347897a32` = `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty. Prediction and observation match exactly, in both direction and cardinality. No dist preflight: the pins import the subject by relative path (`./rest-server.js`), so no package `exports`/`dist` is on the resolution path.

## Verification

Head at the time of every reading below: `d5248b67b8` (`origin/main` merged in at `a016f08b8a`; the merge is a message-only amend of `47a1ecd761`, identical tree `664f0fe0`).

- **Gate families** — derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` from a tree at `origin/main`, reconciled with `--ran`: **58 derived, 58 run, 0 UNRUN**. Exit codes captured by redirect-then-`$?`, never through a pipe.
- **56 of 58 green.** Two returned exit **3 `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`** — `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` — both because they read built output for the whole workspace and this container has no full `pnpm build`. ⛔ Recorded as NOT MEASURED, not as failures and not as passes; CI builds the closure first and is where they get their reading.
- **`pnpm lint`** (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, the whole repo — no narrowing) exit **0** at `d5248b67b8`.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`** — 185 files / **3073 tests**, all pass. The new file contributes 14. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck`) exit 0, 0 debt entries.
- **`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/rest^...' build`** (the dependency closure, downstream direction not applicable — no exported type moves) exit 0.
- **Docs drift** — the automated run covered **none** of this diff; see the dedicated section below for what was hand-swept instead.

## Docs drift — the run produced NO anchor, so this was swept by hand

⛔ **This is not a clean bill of health, and the drift comment says so itself.** The bot reports that **1 changed file yielded no anchor** — `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, which is the only source file in this diff — so *"the pages documenting them are NOT COVERED by this run"*. `scripts/docs-audit/check-affected-docs.mjs` and `check-drift-comment.mjs` do exit 0, but a zero from an instrument whose anchor derivation produced nothing for the file under change is not a reading. `--json` confirms it numerically: `anchors: 0`, `docs: 0`, `detail: 0`, `anchorlessChanges: ["packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts"]`.

⚠️ The **input-vs-emitter** blind spot the bot discloses is live here: this diff is emitter-only, and a page that states a rule by its *inputs* shares no token with the emitter, so it cannot be listed on this run **or any run**. The sweep below was therefore done by CONTENT, over the whole of `content/docs/`, not by anchor.

**What was searched, and the positive control.** Terms: the route itself (`state/:field`, `/state/`, `legalNextStates`), the literal it emits (`Object not found`), the new answer (`503`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `AuthzStoreUnavailable`), the input-side spellings (`no data plane`, `without a data engine`, `objectql not registered`, `no engine is wired`), and every page carrying both `404` and `/meta`.

⭐ **The control fires, and fires exactly where the tooling is blind.** The content sweep found `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx:127`, which documents this very route verbatim — and that page appears in **neither** the anchor run (0 anchors) **nor** the 13-row coarse fallback. It also found `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx:298`, the only non-release page in the tree that names `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` at all, likewise in neither list. A search that reaches two pages both automated paths miss is a search that could have returned a falsification.

**Result: one candidate, reported not edited; nothing else falsified.**

⚠️ **CANDIDATE — `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx:298`.** It reads, inside a comment describing `resolveExecutionContext()`:

> It rejects with AuthzStoreUnavailableError (503) only when an authorization input exists and could not be read — a failed permission-store read, or a tenancy service that is registered and failed to build.

Under the **scoped** reading — a statement about `resolveExecutionContext()`, the function named on the next line — it is untouched: this PR does not change that function, which lives in `packages/runtime`. Under the **global** reading — "that error is only ever raised where an authorization input exists" — **this PR is the first change that makes it false**, because `wiredEngineOrLoud` had exactly one caller until now (`computeExecCtx`, an authorization-input seam) and this adds a second on a **metadata read**, where the engine is consulted as the registry and no capability judgement was being sought. Proposed correction, for whoever owns that page: bound the sentence to `resolveExecutionContext` explicitly, or add that the REST metadata plane raises the same branded error when a wired engine cannot be resolved. ⛔ Not edited here — `content/docs/**` is outside this PR's declared 3-file surface.

**Read and found NOT falsified:**

- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx:127` — the page that documents this exact route. It describes only the **200** answer body (`object, field, from, next`, and when `next` is `null`), which this PR pins unchanged. Not falsified; it is silent on every non-200 answer, which is a pre-existing gap rather than drift.
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx:174` — *"Object not found" after defining it*, the one page keyed on this route's 404 literal. Its three listed causes stay true, it is scoped to `client.data.find`, and it does not claim to be exhaustive. If anything this PR makes it more nearly complete on the `/meta` state route, by removing a fourth cause it never listed.
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx` — documents `/meta` type listings and single-item reads; never mentions the state route and states no 404-versus-503 rule for `/meta`.
- **All 13 coarse-fallback rows read out** (`packageMentionDocs` at `c17b494dba2cf8220dbf6332eedcfbd92305c499`), not dismissed as wide. Eleven contain none of this change's surface terms. `content/docs/api/index.mdx:217` carries only the generic mapping `503 to SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, which this change conforms to. `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` carries the historical v17 notes on the store-outage repair; their explicit "what did NOT change, and is pinned" list (reachable-but-empty store, genuine denial, unprovisioned tables, anonymous callers) is untouched by this PR, and release notes are never edited from a code PR in any case.

**What this sweep does NOT cover:** pages that restate the rule in wording sharing no token with any of the searched terms. That residue is irreducible for an emitter-only diff — it is the #11430 shape the bot names — and it is stated here rather than papered over.

## Changeset — MEASURED, not guessed

`skip-changeset` is refused on evidence. `@objectstack/rest` was built and `npm pack --dry-run --json` run; the changed route's own literal (`State-machine introspection is not available in this runtime`) was searched across **every packed path** the pack reported (10 files), not against the `files[]` field:

- POSITIVE CONTROL fires in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs` ⇒ this route ships.
- NEGATIVE CONTROL (a nonsense symbol) fires nowhere ⇒ the search discriminates.

⇒ `.changeset/meta-state-route-engine-outage-distinguishable.md`, `@objectstack/rest: patch`.

## Clause ② — re-derived from the delivered diff, not copied

`Clause-②: no`.

- **No accept set widens.** Nothing that was refused becomes served: the two absence rows keep their 404, the healthy-engine rows are untouched, and the only movement is *which refusal is named* for a fault that was already being refused. `POST /email/send` moves 500 → 501, refusal to refusal.
- **No published surface grows.** No new route, no new export, and **no new wire code**: `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` is an existing `StandardErrorCode` member, reached through the existing `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` — `authz-store-unavailable.ts` says so itself: *"Deliberately NOT a new code: the wire vocabulary is closed."*
- **It is a pull-back to a declared contract**, which the criterion says does not touch clause ②. The contract is `@objectstack/core`'s published `AUTHZ_STORE_UNAVAILABLE_STATUS = 503` and `wiredEngineOrLoud`'s own table (`the engine cannot be RESOLVED: 403 → 503`).

⚠️ **The second look the dispatch asked for, recorded rather than waved past:** an operator-visible status code *does* move on a published route (404 → 503, multi-kernel wiring). Under the criterion's own negative boundary that is a runtime refusal-path behaviour change, not an accept-set widening — hence `no`. A reviewer who reads the boundary the other way should say so; the basis is stated here so it can be overturned on the record rather than re-derived.

## 验收备注

- ⛔ **Deliberately not widened.** `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts` was read only. The provider closures there belong to #14251 phase 1 and are untouched.
- **Noted, not filed — a third `objectQLProvider` consumer.** `POST {basePath}/batch` reaches the slot with no `.catch` at all, so a rejection propagates to that handler's own `handleRouteError`. It does **not** carry this card's defect (it never collapses an outage into "not found"), and it was not in the card's enumeration. Whoever next audits the slot's consumer census is the reader for this. Carrier: #14251's census.
- **Noted, not filed — the two consumers ask different sources.** On the multi-kernel wiring the gate resolves the engine from the per-environment kernel while this route asks the local-kernel `objectQLProvider`, which `rest-api-plugin.ts` documents as the *"single-kernel fallback"*. That asymmetry is what makes the defect reachable at all; it is a wiring question one layer above this file and is not touched here. Carrier: the same census.
